newsitem.title: USA: 7th Level software CEO quits; to focus on video games.
newsitem.headline: 7th Level software CEO quits; to focus on video games.

text.p: 7th Level Inc., an educational software company in which Michael Milken is a major investor, said Tuesday that its chairman and chief executive quit and that his replacements will refocus the company on writing more video games.
Dallas-based 7th Level said George Grayson resigned and named Donald Schupak, a business consultant and board member, as chairman. The company also named Bob Ezrin, its president, as acting CEO.

Until now, 7th Level has concentrated on writing software to help children learn reading and writing. The company attracted Milken -- the former junk-bond trader who now likes to invest in companies developing technology for education -- as an investor.
Milken owns about 15 percent of 7th Level's stock.
7th Level now will concentrate on using its expertise in 3-D graphics software to write more video games, a more lucrative business, Schupak said.
"My job is to turn these wonderful assets into profit," he said. "I would be suprised and disappointed if in a year from now 7th Level was not a darling again."

Like other consumer software companies, 7th Level has faced collapsing software prices and competition for shelf space at retailers. Its stock has slid more than 80 percent from a high of $22 in September 1995, ending Tuesday at $4, up 81 cents, on Nasdaq.
Schupak said he had not spoken to Milken about the company's new focus. A spokesman for Milken's investment firm said he could not comment.
